user.title: Battery Opt
user.description: Prices come from Home Assistant's own OMIE integration - set it up first (Settings > Devices & services > Add > OMIE). This form is house-level only: meter sensors (all optional - everything degrades gracefully until they are set) and the planning parameters. Batteries are added afterwards from the integration page via 'Add battery' (each battery is its own sub-entry with its marstek_modbus entities, power sensor, capacity and self-discharge); with no battery the integration runs in planning-only mode.

data.load_sensor: House load sensor (power W or energy kWh, optional)
data.grid_power_sensor: Grid import power sensor (W, charge-power loop)
data.capacity_kwh: Usable capacity (kWh) - planning-only fallback; each battery sub-entry carries its own
data.self_discharge_w: Standby self-discharge (W) - planning-only fallback; each battery sub-entry carries its own
data.dry_run: Dry-run (Task 12): keep actuating the static plan; the greedy stays advisory. Disable only after Checkpoint C

error.omie_not_set_up: The OMIE integration is not set up. Add it first: Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > OMIE.
error.timezone_not_lisbon: Home Assistant's timezone must be Europe/Lisbon: the tariff calendar, the OMIE market day and every trigger are Portugal-local. Change it under Settings > System > General.

get_best_periods.name: Get best periods
get_best_periods.description: Returns the cheap periods of a day's delivered prices — the best times to run high-power appliances. Each period is a maximal stretch of consecutive cheap quarter-hours (at or below the day's minimum plus the threshold share of its price range), listed in time order with start, end and average delivered price, plus the day's average and the cheap cutoff used.

day.name: Day
day.description: Which day to rank: today, or tomorrow once OMIE has published it (~13:30 CET).

min_duration.name: Minimum duration
min_duration.description: Cheap stretches shorter than this are dropped (rounded up to whole quarter-hours).

threshold.name: Threshold
threshold.description: How far above the day's minimum still counts as cheap, as a percentage of the day's price range. 0 keeps only the very cheapest quarters; larger values widen the periods.

count.name: Number of periods
count.description: How many periods at most; the cheapest by average are kept, listed in time order.

after.name: After
after.description: Only consider periods starting at or after this time of day (cheapness is judged within these bounds).

before.name: Before
before.description: Only consider periods ending at or before this time of day.

user.title: Add battery
user.description: One battery of the fleet: its marstek_modbus control entities (enable force_mode, rs485_control_mode, set_charge_power and charge_to_soc upstream first - user_work_mode is enabled by default), its own power sensor (W - the charge loop and realised savings need EVERY battery's), and its physical parameters. The cutoff numbers do not exist on the Venus E V3: leave them empty there.

data.battery_power_sensor: This battery's power sensor (W, HA convention: positive = discharging)

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure battery
reconfigure.description: Edit this battery's entities and physical parameters; the integration reloads on save.
